title: StellarWave Renewal & Regional Capacity Planning
summary: Renewal conversation focused on increasing reserved capacity, adding an EU region, and options for a short private pilot for data residency. Customer is leaning toward a 12-month committed uplift with burst credit. Action items include latency benchmarks, updated pricing, and legal/procurement paperwork timeline.
action_items: Samir Rao: run 24h tail-latency and 99th-percentile throughput benchmark against their promo prompt set and share results (due 2025-08-28)
Lena Ortiz: provide 12-month committed pricing sheet with burst credit example and cost per 1M tokens (due 2025-08-25)
Priya Menon: schedule Private pilot scoping call with Security + Infra (StellarWave) and attach SOC2 + ISO docs (due 2025-08-26)
Jordan Lee / Tom Rivers: share internal firewall egress rules and preferred VPC peering window (due 2025-08-23)
Marta Silva: confirm procurement timeline and PO requirement checklist (due 2025-08-29)
next_steps: Run Redwood-managed latency test against their nightly job and share spreadsheet
Deliver updated proposal with committed uplift options (6 vs 12 months) and EU region add-on
Start security scoping for private pilot (if procurement approves)
Follow-up sync next week to review benchmarks and finalize term
transcript:
[00:00] Lena Ortiz: Hey everyone, thanks for joining — appreciate you making time. Quick check, audio ok?
[00:08] Jordan Lee: Yep, loud and clear, thanks Lena.
[00:12] Priya Menon: Quick intro: I'm Priya, CSM on the account, I'll help run the pilot and onboarding bits.
[00:22] Aisha Khan: Aisha here — product owner, want to make sure latency doesn't regress as we expand.
[00:28] Tom Rivers: Tom, DevOps, I'll coordinate Infra stuff.
[00:31] Lena Ortiz: Great. High-level agenda: renewal options, capacity uplift, adding EU region, and discuss private/VPC pilot for residency. Want to capture timelines for procurement.
[00:45] Jordan Lee: Sounds good. To start — our usage has jumped steady over the last quarter, burst traffic at EOD is the problem. 95th is fine but tail latency spikes, and sometimes KV cache warm-up kills a few minutes.
[01:04] Samir Rao: Understood. When you say KV cache warm-up, is that during new sessions or after long inactivity windows?
[01:11] Jordan Lee: Mostly after less used flows, like our reverse-rerank pipeline that runs at 11pm PST. It floods with long sequences.
[01:19] Samir Rao: Ok, that helps. We can tune continuous batching and cache warmup; for Dedicated you can pin warm WUs — also quantization profiles help reduce per-token cost.
[01:35] Aisha Khan: Can you remind us the primary difference for failure modes between hosted and Dedicated? We saw a link in the deck but want plain talk.
[01:44] Lena Ortiz: Sure — hosted is the fastest to scale but shared pools so noisy neighbor risk exists (we mitigate it with routing and fallbacks). Dedicated gives predictable throughput and isolation, cost is higher but latency SLOs are stronger and you get explicit SLA. Also reserved capacity includes burst credits for spikes.
[02:07] Tom Rivers: And Private deployment — that's a different beast?
[02:10] Samir Rao: Private gives you VPC/on-prem options, customer-managed network, and KMS integration for keys. But it requires extra lead time and infra readiness — usually a pilot of 4–6 weeks for onboarding.
[02:24] Jordan Lee: On lead time — our procurement needs potential go-live for EU region by mid-October. Is that realistic?
[02:31] Lena Ortiz: Mid-October could be tight but doable if we start security scoping this week and agree on capacity. We would schedule region activation and a configuration freeze for the model variants.
[02:44] Marta Silva: From procurement: timeline aside, we need a clear PO value and three vendor docs: SOC2, contract redlines, and a data residency addendum. Do you have those ready?
[02:55] Priya Menon: Yes — I will attach SOC2 and ISO artifacts. For data residency we have a template addendum. We'll send those after the call.
[03:06] Jordan Lee: Perfect. Also curious about fallback strategy — if EU region overloads can we failover to US with reduced capacity? We need predictable service.
[03:16] Samir Rao: Yes, smart routing allows policy-based fallback. You can set region, cost, or latency preference; automatic fallback to a compatible model family is standard. There is potential output variance between model variants; we'll show you example diffs.
[03:32] Aisha Khan: About model variants — we rely on a specific open model right now, if fallback moves to a quantized variant, how big are the regressions?
[03:40] Samir Rao: Usually small for re-ranking tasks; for generation where prompt sensitivity is high, we recommend an eval set. Redwood Optimize can surface regression alerts tied to your prompts.
[03:52] Jordan Lee: Great — we do have a regression test harness. We'll share it.
[03:56] Lena Ortiz: On pricing: we put together committed tiers — 6 months vs 12 months — and burst credits. For many customers the 12-month gives a better unit cost. I'll send a concrete sheet.
[04:06] Marta Silva: We prefer 12-months for budget predictability but need cancellation clauses if SLA not met.
[04:13] Lena Ortiz: Noted — we can include SLA credits language. We'll loop legal if you want redline suggestions.
[04:21] Jordan Lee: Can you walk through an example cost for 10M tokens a day with EU region active?
[04:27] Samir Rao: Sure — rough math: base per-token on committed tier plus EU egress and region multiplier. I'll include two worked examples in the proposal: one for hosted multi-region and one for dedicated EU+US.
[04:42] Aisha Khan: About private pilot — we need KMS and HSM support plus audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. Is that supported?
[04:51] Samir Rao: Yes — Private supports customer KMS, HSM integration, and audit log exports. The SIEM integration goes through secure syslog or cloud-native connectors; we'll have engineering scope it.
[05:03] Tom Rivers: Any required open ports or egress rules for the pilot?
[05:07] Priya Menon: We'll provide a firewall checklist; typical is outbound to specific IP ranges and a few management endpoints. Jordan/Tom, please share your egress window.
[05:18] Jordan Lee: We'll share.
[05:20] Lena Ortiz: Quick re-ask — what's success criteria for the renewal?
[05:24] Aisha Khan: For us: 1) 12-month committed uplift approved, 2) EU region live by mid-October, 3) tail latency 99th < 300ms for main flows, 4) private pilot scoped and security sign-off.
[05:39] Lena Ortiz: Good, that helps a lot. I'm going to flag the 99th-ms SLA — we can aim for that with Dedicated and right batching/cache. We'll validate with bench.
[05:49] Samir Rao: For the bench I'll need the prompt set and the rerank flow. Also helpful: sequence lengths distribution and concurrency patterns.
[05:57] Jordan Lee: We'll upload a sample job and sequence histogram to the shared drive.
[06:01] Marta Silva: Procurement question — are there pre-paid invoices or monthly billing? We prefer PO + net30 invoicing.
[06:08] Lena Ortiz: We support both; for committed reserved capacity we can accept PO + net30 and provide invoice schedule.
[06:16] Tom Rivers: On the pilot side, if we do Private, are you handling the infra or we bring our own?
[06:22] Samir Rao: There's a spectrum — VPC-hosted private: Redwood manages control plane with customer VPC peering; on-prem: more work on your side. We'll propose the VPC-hosted pilot unless you prefer fully on-prem.
[06:36] Jordan Lee: VPC-hosted sounds safer for timeline.
[06:40] Aisha Khan: For the EU region, do you support data residency in the cloud provider of our choice? We use EU AWS accounts.
[06:48] Priya Menon: Yes — we can deploy into your cloud region and support KMS in your account for keys.
[06:54] Jordan Lee: On SLAs: what's the typical credit if SLO missed?
[06:58] Lena Ortiz: Usually credits tied to uptime and 99th latency windows; we'll put the exact figures in the contract redline.
[07:06] Tom Rivers: We need an ops runbook too — how Redwood suggests we do failovers and cache warm-up.
[07:11] Samir Rao: We'll provide a runbook with suggested traffic-shaping, pre-warming hooks, and prefix caching. There is also an API to snapshot KV cache across sessions for faster warm-up.
[07:24] Jordan Lee: Interesting — snapshot KV cache, is that automated?
[07:28] Samir Rao: There's an endpoint for exporting and seeding caches; we can walk you through it during onboarding.
[07:35] Aisha Khan: Great. Procurement-wise, Marta — what's the approval window?
[07:39] Marta Silva: We need signed PO by 09/05 to meet budget cycle. If we hit that, mid-October activation is still on track.
[07:48] Lena Ortiz: Good to know. We'll aim for a signed PO cadence.
[07:52] Priya Menon: I'll start the security scoping invite and attach SOC2 + ISO docs after the call.
[07:59] Jordan Lee: On benchmarks, are you able to run things from our EU region to avoid cross-region noise?
[08:04] Samir Rao: Yes — we can route tests via the EU cluster; need temporary access to test harness and endpoints.
[08:12] Jordan Lee: We'll provide that.
[08:15] Aisha Khan: One more question — if we commit to 12 months and traffic drops, is there flexibility to downscale?
[08:22] Lena Ortiz: Contracts usually have re-provision windows; we'll propose a carve-out for a small downscale after Q2 with a reprice. I'll outline options in the proposal.
[08:34] Tom Rivers: Also want to confirm observability — does the Console provide token-level cost per route?
[08:39] Samir Rao: Yes, token-level cost and per-route latency breakdowns, plus trace hooks. You'll get role-based access too.
[08:47] Jordan Lee: Good.
[08:50] Marta Silva: Regarding legal, any standard indemnity clauses we should watch for?
[08:54] Lena Ortiz: We'll send a standard SOW and MSA, happy to accept reasonable redlines. Priya will coordinate legal.
[09:02] Samir Rao: Back to technical — for quantization, if you run 4-bit profiles we can save cost but need to validate quality. We'll include example outputs.
[09:11] Aisha Khan: Yes please do.
[09:13] Lena Ortiz: Quick recap items — benchmarks, pricing sheet, security docs, procurement checklist, and a follow-up next week.
[09:21] Jordan Lee: Works for us.
[09:23] Priya Menon: I'll send the calendar invite for the security scoping and attach docs.
[09:28] Lena Ortiz: Marta, Jordan — any blockers from procurement or budget to flag now?
[09:33] Marta Silva: No blockers beyond timeline; just need the PO amount and the invoice cadence.
[09:38] Lena Ortiz: Ok. I'll push the proposal with two committed options and the EU add-on; Samir will attach the bench plan.
[09:46] Tom Rivers: Thanks — can we get the bench run before next Wed?
[09:49] Samir Rao: We'll attempt a bench window over the weekend; results early next week.
[09:55] Aisha Khan: If we see regressions, is rollback fast?
[09:58] Samir Rao: Yes, rollouts support canary and automatic fallback. We'll include a test plan.
[10:06] Jordan Lee: Great, thanks everyone.
[10:10] Lena Ortiz: Thanks all, we'll follow up with artifacts. End.
